findings.claim: Quoting line 30: "gpu-q refuses, with a non-zero exit and before taking the lock, a locked command whose argv is a bare cargo test / cargo build / cargo nextest run without a prior --no-run build." The done_when is owner-free and falsifiable, baseline is measured (#3986), but the first-green proof tests only gpu-q externally and fails to prevent bare flock bypasses in repo scripts.
findings.fix: Add an in-repo CI check/wrapper ensuring no script runs bare flock /tmp/apr-gpu.lock or compiles under the lock.

findings.claim: Quoting line 40: "scripts/gpu_lock_idle_sample.sh samples utilization at 1 Hz while the lock is held, and writes {host, window, samples, idle_fraction, holders[]}." The done_when is owner-free and falsifiable, baseline is honestly cited as no instrument exists (#3986), and proof verifies calculations and 0-sample errors, but lacks a test ensuring daemon terminates upon lock release.
findings.fix: Add a test asserting that the sampling daemon terminates cleanly immediately upon lock release to prevent orphaned processes.

findings.claim: Quoting line 49: "scripts/model_ladder.sh CPU legs (--no-gpu, -ngl 0 -dev none) and its sha256 pass run without apr_locked/gpu-q. GPU legs are unchanged." The done_when is owner-free and falsifiable, baseline is cited (#3986 P3), and the first-green proof is non-vacuous (mutant is caught).
findings.fix: Implement as written; ensure the flag parser regex covers all CPU flag variants and prevents lock acquisition for CPU-only rungs.

findings.claim: Quoting line 59: "The release train pre-freeze stage runs the risk cells on an idle card of the same compute capability as each release host (sm_89 for lambda, sm_121 for gx10)." The done_when is compromised by an informal ticketing dependency ("before it is ticketed") and an impossible sm_121 idle host, while the first-green proof is vacuous because it only validates receipt headers rather than asserting execution of risk cells.
findings.fix: Automate reproduction without human ticketing clauses, remove nonexistent sm_121 idle host requirement (or provision one), and assert executed risk cell count > 0 in the receipt.

findings.claim: Quoting line 76: "the ladder sweep partitions its cells across the hosts that can run them, and one reducer merges the shards into ONE receipt per release host." The done_when is owner-free and falsifiable, baseline is stated, and proof tests reducer rejection of bad shards, but definition of architecture-independent cells is unstated.
findings.fix: Specify the exact contract and metadata filter identifying which cells are architecture-independent and eligible for migration.

findings.claim: Quoting line 98: "The pilot does NOT change the lock policy (see Q4)." The done_when and first-green proof are falsifiable, but the row provides zero operational benefit or speedup for release 0.70 while risking GPU stability during sweeps.
findings.fix: Defer FT-6 to release 0.71 or 0.72 as out-of-scope for the 0.70 Fast Train release.

findings.claim: Quoting line 103: "(b) the serve probe keeps its own evidence (#3949, already merged; this row is its regression guard staying wired)." The done_when is falsifiable for (a) and (c), but sub-item (b) has no baseline in lines 105-107 and no first-green proof in lines 108-112.
findings.fix: Supply the missing baseline for (b) and add a first-green proof asserting that the serve probe evidence file is generated, non-empty, and preserved.

findings.claim: Quoting line 127: "The baseline starts at the measured dark count, and can only go down." The done_when is owner-free, baseline is measured at 49fe19c28, but the first-green proof is vacuous: a shrink-only baseline allows 0.70 to pass without compiling any dark tests. Furthermore, first-green proofs for #3984 and #3982 are omitted.
findings.fix: Enforce that the shrink-only dark baseline must reach zero at release freeze, and add explicit first-green compilation tests for #3984 and #3982.

findings.claim: Quoting line 136: "apr validate --quality F exits non-zero or is documented as not a gate." The done_when contains an evasion loophole allowing un-gated failures if documented, though baselines and drain guard first-green proofs are otherwise solid.
findings.fix: Remove the "or is documented as not a gate" escape hatch; require strict non-zero exits for all release gates.

findings.claim: Quoting line 147: "the train ledger records freeze_at (the release branch cut) and published_at (crates.io + the GH release, the later of the two) from the automation." The done_when is owner-free and falsifiable, baseline gap is honestly noted, and first-green proof is non-vacuous.
findings.fix: Implement as written, ensuring freeze_at is written immutably during the branch cut.

findings.claim: Quoting line 156: "This row carries only what 0.69.1 did not close." The done_when is falsifiable and baselines are cited, but carrying low-bit admission kernels and MoE CUDA fixes into 0.70 threatens the <= 4h train speed goal.
findings.fix: Move all low-bit admission kernels and MoE CUDA fixes to 0.71 "Don't Leave Behind", retaining only the #3951 RED-MODEL attribution oracle in 0.70.

findings.claim: Quoting line 167: "[U] until aprender-cb sizing lands. The thresholds are copied into this row verbatim in a follow-up commit on this PR." The done_when violates the owner-free requirement by naming a person, the text omits Pillar B's baseline entirely, numeric thresholds are missing, and the proof is vacuous.
findings.fix: Incorporate explicit numeric thresholds for all pillars A-D directly into the specification, remove personal ownership references, and supply the baseline for Pillar B.

findings.claim: Quoting line 162: "baselines (from #3997, to be re-derived by aprender-cb commands): - A: 88.78 % line (COV_FLOOR := 88); - C: 13/27 ONT rows bound; - D: 715 open issues (121 with no milestone), 57 open PRs, 2,594 remote branches (2026-09-23 09:50Z)." The baseline for Pillar B (pv depth) is completely missing from the plan.
findings.fix: Measure and document the current 0.69.x pv depth baseline in the FT-12 baselines block.

findings.claim: Ran ls -la .quorum/ which returned "No such file or directory" (exit 2). Acceptance criterion #3 of PMAT-3998 requires: "A 3-lane quorum ... reviews the plan and decides the epic's open questions; its receipt is committed beside the plan." The receipt directory .quorum/PMAT-3998/ does not exist.
findings.fix: Create .quorum/PMAT-3998/ and commit the 3-lane quorum review receipts alongside the plan.

findings.claim: Ran grep -rn "apr-gpu.lock" scripts/ and inspected scripts/model_ladder.sh:77: "apr_locked() { flock -E \"$LOCK_BUSY\" -w \"$LOCK_WAIT\" \"$GPU_LOCK\" choom -n 1000 -- \"$APR\" \"$@\"; }". Repo scripts bypass gpu-q with bare flock calls, making FT-1's external gpu-q check ineffective against in-tree code.
findings.fix: Update scripts/model_ladder.sh and CI scripts to route through the compliant gpu_test.sh harness rather than invoking bare flock directly.

findings.claim: Quoting line 76: "The hosts are lambda, gx10 and yoga (CUDA), plus the Mac host (CPU/Metal legs only; it has no CUDA)." The fleet contains only one sm_121 host (gx10); yoga and lambda are sm_89. Therefore, FT-4's requirement to run pre-screen risk cells on an "idle card of the same compute capability ... sm_121 for gx10" is impossible with existing fleet hosts.
findings.fix: Either adjust FT-4 to exempt unique hardware architectures or explicitly provision a secondary sm_121 instance.
